source.title: steering-vector distillation
source.authors: C. Blank; A. Bhatia; Senthooran Rajamanoharan; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The study repeats the filtered teacher-output/student-fine-tuning pipeline and preference evaluation, while testing it across models and conditions and adding causal steering-vector interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports cross-model steering-vector effects on loss and extensive mechanistic measurements. Cross-model loss reduction is not itself a measurement of trait transmission, so those results are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as evidence for the same-base behavioral claim. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reruns the Cloud et al. pipeline (system-prompted teacher, filtered number sequences, LoRA student, preference evaluation) on Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-3-4b, Llama-3.1-8B and OLMo-3-7B. It reports trait hit rates (A) and adds causal steering-vector, gradient and optimizer tests (D). It also compares full fine-tuning with several LoRA ranks and alphas (E). Cross-model results are loss-only, so B is not tested behaviourally.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that LLM subliminal learning is mediated by a single steering vector, as a special case of steering vector distillation. Only steerable traits transfer, and they argue that model-specific vector effects explain the lack of cross-model transfer. The effect needs LoRA with adaptive optimizers and was absent under full FT and SGD in their system-prompt tests. They add that steering-vector distillation still occurs, more weakly, under full FT. They also state the account is not exhaustive.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the original three-stage teacher-output/student-fine-tuning design with filtered number sequences and preference evaluation, then adds vector steering/ablation, code and paraphrase settings, and optimizer/training-recipe comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with trait steerability, teacher/student model, training duration, LoRA versus full fine-tuning, optimizer, and tested LoRA rank/scaling. The text also reports weaker subliminal learning for Gemma than Qwen.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering directions reduce NLL on the same model's completions. OLMo directions raise loss on Qwen numbers. Within the OLMo family (Instruct/Think), all four data→scorer cells reduce loss, e.g. 61.3% and 57.3% on semantic data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-specific components of steering directions predict data likelihood mainly within a model family. This is a loss result offered as an explanation for B, not a behavioural test.

fits_no_version.finding: In the MNIST MLP, bias-only distillation of auxiliary logits leaves accuracy near 10%, while full-weight distillation succeeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The steering-vector account does not explain subliminal learning in MLPs.

record.problems: The authors state that vector addition does not fully recover the Qwen effect and vector removal does not fully eliminate it, so the account is not exhaustive. They report limited data points, weaker effects for Gemma, and less salient Qwen results at 10 epochs. Several plotted outcomes are not numerically specified in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports further figure-based optimizer variants, full-fine-tuning steering-vector-distillation metrics, and multiple cross-model steering/loss comparisons (Figures 5b, 7c, 16, 18 and Appendix K). They are not separately rowed here because the cross-model results are loss metrics rather than direct trait-transmission rates, while the remaining figure-only comparisons are supplementary to the extracted core results.

untested.parts: Maths/chain-of-thought outputs are not tested. Only system-prompted and (Appendix E) fine-tuned teachers are used.
No student is trained on a different-base teacher's filtered outputs with its trait rate measured. Only loss reduction under cross-model steering is reported.
Misalignment and other harmful traits are not tested.
Evaluation-prompt variation beyond the standard held-out preference questions is not tested. Full-FT trait rates for system-prompted teachers are reported only for cats.
No prompt-only token insertion is tested. Activation steering is not a prompt-only analogue.

missing.what: Steerability predicts which traits are learned across 16 animals: AUC 0.86 for Qwen, 0.91 for Llama, 1.00 for OLMo.
v_student sufficiency and necessity across five LoRA configurations; ablation removes nearly all of the effect.
Full-FT steering-vector distillation: shift rates lower than under LoRA, EAS above 0.3 for all traits.
Fine-tuned-teacher mechanism numbers: v_teacher steering gives 50%, v_student steering 58%, ablation removes over 80%.
Adding v_teacher lowers NLL/token from 0.7273 to 0.6823, about 32% of the gap to the system-prompt roofline.
Optimizer variants (RMSProp, SGD+momentum, per-parameter SGD, bottom-10% frozen, rotated) and their cat hit rates.
Mean-centred teacher and student vectors match per trait: diagonal cosine about 0.29–0.36, off-diagonal near 0.

record.verdict_notes: Most rows are figure-only with no numbers stated in the text. The 'held-out evaluation' support label for E was dropped: evaluating on preference questions is the standard design, not a robustness test. Concurrent work (ref 24) reportedly finds SGD can work with tuning; the authors could not replicate it.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test every possible unrelated output type or every filtering procedure.

It does not directly train a student on filtered outputs from a teacher with a different base model and measure the student's trait preference. Cross-model steering-vector loss results are not a direct transmission-rate test.
The paper does not test transmission of misalignment or another alignment-relevant harmful trait.
The study tests the steering-vector account and an optimizer/gradient explanation, but does not experimentally adjudicate the token-entanglement or divergence-token accounts.
The study tests full fine-tuning, several LoRA rank/scaling configurations, and held-out preference prompts; it does not establish robustness to all training recipes or evaluation sets.
No linked-token prompt-only intervention without fine-tuning is tested. Activation steering is not a prompt-only analogue.

source_check.notes: The text has no capability evaluation, so the call's capability=y and the 'capability check' claims in D.support[1] and the reading list are unsupported. No rows record: Figure 10 (system-prompted students across five LoRA configs; v_student ablation removes nearly all); Figure 7b's LoRA+Adam effect in Llama and OLMo; Appendix N (bias-only steering fails in the MNIST MLP, a D scope limit); the authors' failure to replicate 2606.00831's SGD transfer. Steering-vector runs use 100k generations vs 10k.

statements.correction: arXiv:2606.00995: R14 is Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, code carrier, cat trait, substring plus GPT 5.4-nano filter (figure only). R15 is Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, paraphrased Alpaca, tiger trait (figure only). 95% Wilson CIs over 500 samples; code released; preprint; T1.
statements.problem: The visible text gives no detail for this study. The conditions' student list omits Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (the R15 paraphrase student), and the 'why' does not describe this study.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: the four traits with a 0.0% inference-time steering rate (raccoons, rabbits, giraffes, frogs) were not learned. Peacock was not learned after 2 epochs but was learned after 10 epochs (Section 4.1).
statements.problem: Omits that peacock was learned after 10 epochs, at a rate similar to its steering rate. For peacock the varying factor is training length, not the choice of animal.

statements.correction: R33: on the same 10k-sample Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct numbers data, peacock is not learned after 2 epochs but is learned after 10 epochs, so more epochs help here.
statements.problem: The part of the statement about this study is cut off in the pack, so it can't be checked.

statements.correction: R16: a fine-tuned cat teacher (400 QA pairs, 3 epochs) gives 19.2% cat preference after 9 student epochs, lower than with a system-prompted teacher; the v_teacher/v_student mechanism still holds. R8: data from a v_teacher-steered Gemma-3-4b-it teacher induce subliminal learning (Gemma is weaker overall).
statements.problem: The text about this study is cut off. Its cited rows show weaker transfer, not absent transfer, so they fit limits_scope rather than a 'challenges' label.

Accurate, but omits context: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, after 9 epochs, lower than with the system-prompted teacher.

statements.correction: No capability evaluation is reported. The only related check is negative evaluation prompts, keeping the negative-preference rate <10% when steering Llama/OLMo (Appendix G). Random/SAE vectors: distillation shown by loss, activation cosine and EAS.
statements.problem: The 'why' claims a capability check, but none is in the text. Random vectors were not evaluated behaviourally (semantic shift is measured only for semantic vectors).

statements.correction: R20: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct reference model. cos(g_clean - g_teacher, v_teacher) at the assistant tag, averaged over up to 1024 prompts, is small and consistently positive (figure only).
statements.problem: The text about this study is cut off in the pack.

statements.correction: Section 3.2: replacing the v_student component removes over 50% of trait behaviour (Figure 3, Qwen and Gemma, not split by model). Appendix E: over 80% removed with a fine-tuned teacher.
statements.problem: 'Over 50%' is not Qwen-specific in the text. No Gemma-specific 'suppresses rather than removes' finding exists; 'suppresses' is the Introduction's general wording.

statements.correction: 2606.00995 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with number sequences: 16 animals, inference-time v_teacher steering predicts which traits students learn (Appendix G, Figure 15b; correlational, not ablation). LoRA+Adam exceeds the reference in Llama (Figure 7b). v_teacher comes from the system prompt; v_student is the student's fine-tuning-induced shift.
statements.problem: Says this study uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct only for paraphrased Alpaca. It also uses it with number sequences from system-prompted teachers. v_student is a fine-tuning shift, not a vector derived from the system prompt.
Accurate. Trait is cat.

statements.correction: Section 3.3: ablating v_teacher removes nearly all of the effect. Section 3.2: v_student replacement removes over 50% (main config). Figure 10b: nearly all removed across five LoRA configs. Appendix E: over 80% (fine-tuned teacher).
statements.problem: Cites this study as a case where single interventions remove only part of transfer. Its v_teacher ablation removes nearly all, and v_student ablation removes nearly all in the other LoRA configs.
Accurate (loss-matched: SGD loss 0.167, Adam loss 0.142).
